# Compatible Minkowski interpolation does not linearize physical cap losses

This note proves an exact closure of actual compatible families, then
gives a nonsmooth obstruction to treating its cap responses as convex
averages. The obstruction uses actual globally critical original caps,
not an arbitrary signed functional. It does not claim that no other
convexification of compatible first motions is possible.

## 1. Exact compatible interpolation

Let two families K_z^1(e),K_z^2(e) on the same finite complete integer
base satisfy every actual anchored inclusion, and have the same
original fibers K_z at e=0. For fixed 0<=t<=1 put

    L_z(e)=(1-t)K_z^1(e)+t K_z^2(e).                     (1)

Then every anchored representation satisfies

    sum_z lambda_z L_z(e)
      =(1-t)sum_z lambda_z K_z^1(e)
           +t sum_z lambda_z K_z^2(e)
      subset (1-t)K_q^1(e)+tK_q^2(e)=L_q(e).             (2)

Thus the exact fiber hull realizes these interpolated fibers. Positivity
and nesting in K_z are preserved. The standard rational perpendicular
thickening handles deficient base rank without changing integer fibers.
No pointwise one-input field inequality is needed for this closure.

Support functions average exactly in(1). Actual removed-volume and cap
first variations, however, need not average. A flat exposed face permits
different original points of that same face to be combined.

## 2. An exact nonsmooth facet computation

Let K=[-1,1]^2. For 0<e<1 define two nested convex quadrilaterals by

    K1(e)={-1<=x<=1, -1<=y<=1-e(1+x)},
    K2(e)={-1<=x<=1, -1<=y<=1-e(1-x)}.                   (3)

Each has exact area4-2e. At a point x of the upper face, their normal
loss profiles are g1(x)=1+x and g2(x)=1-x. A point in their half-Minkowski
sum has x=(x1+x2)/2, so its maximal y is

    1-e inf{[g1(x1)+g2(x2)]/2:
                  x1,x2 in[-1,1], x1+x2=2x}.

The infimum is |x|: set x1=max(-1,2x-1) and x2=2x-x1. Therefore

    L(e)=(K1(e)+K2(e))/2
        ={-1<=x<=1, -1<=y<=1-e|x|},
    |L(e)|=4-e.                                          (4)

The lower endpoint y=-1 is attainable for every admissible x, and the
vertical section is an interval, proving the ENTIRE set equality in(4).
The averaged physical loss profile would instead be the constant1,
which gives the different rectangle [-1,1]x[-1,1-e], of area4-2e.

For the fixed cap x<=0 the exact losses are

    |K cap H|-|K1(e) cap H|=e/2,
    |K cap H|-|K2(e) cap H|=3e/2,
    |K cap H|-|L(e) cap H|=e/2.                           (5)

The actual interpolated loss is NOT the average e. The cap x>=0 has
the reverse first two losses and the same final e/2. Equations(4)--(5)
are exact finite-parameter identities, not an uncontrolled limiting
argument at a roof knot.

## 3. An actual critical-cover payment reverses sign

Use n=1,d=2 and the complete binary base P={0,1}. At base0 put K as
above, and at base1 put the centrally symmetric rectangle

    B=[-2/3,2/3]x[-1,1], |B|=8/3.

Their fiber hull is an ambient convex body. Binary extreme bases have
no nontrivial anchored relations. At either base, a sufficiently steep
integer tilt isolates any ordinary fiber cap. Hence mixed depth on
that fiber equals ordinary fiber depth, and the actual global raw
maximum is Q=2, attained at the center of K. The total is20/3, so

    beta=3/10.                                           (6)

The actual critical caps

    H^-: -x-2z>=0,   H^+: x-2z>=0                         (7)

each have mass2 and cover the full base0 plane; their base1 traces are
empty. The two caps +/-x+2(z-1)>=0 cover base1 and have mass4/3<Q.
Thus this is a genuine global fixed critical cover with strict slack
at its other base.

In BOTH branches deform B by the SAME actual nested rectangles

    B(e)=[-2/3,2/3]x[-1+3e/8,1-3e/8],
    |B(e)|=8/3-e.                                        (8)

Branch r uses K_r(e) from(3). Both branches, their physical Minkowski
interpolation, and the separately defined averaged-profile rectangle
are actual compatible binary-base families. All cap traces in(7) at
base1 remain empty.

The two branches each have total first loss3. The CONVEX AVERAGE of
their two critical-row loss vectors is(1,1), so treating responses as
linear would give positive payment

    1-beta*3=1/10                                         (9)

for EVERY critical row. This vector is indeed realized by the separate
averaged-profile rectangle path. That path has exact global depth
(2-e)/(20/3-3e)<3/10 for small positive e, since its base0 body remains
centrally symmetric and the base1 maximum retains its strict gap.

But the actual Minkowski interpolation has total first loss2, and
each SAME critical cap loses only1/2. Its payment is

    1/2-beta*2=-1/10.                                    (10)

Consequently the proposed identification of physical Minkowski
interpolation with convex averaging of first cap responses is false,
even at an actual deepest source with a fixed genuine critical cover
and slack at the other base. Formula(10) is a failure of that cover's
descent certificate. No global-depth formula for the pentagon L(e) is
needed or claimed.

## 4. The missing regularity in a support-function shortcut

For K1(e), consider the fixed unnormalized normal (eta,1). When eta>0
and e<eta, its support point is the upper-right vertex and

    [h_K(eta,1)-h_K1(e)(eta,1)]/e=2.

At eta=0 the upper-left vertex keeps support value1, and this quotient
is0. For eta<0 it is also0 for small e. After unit normalization the
right limit is still2 whereas the value at the upper normal is0.
Thus the support-difference quotients do not converge uniformly to a
continuous function on the normal circle. Looking only at the original
facet's support value would miss its entire area loss2e.

There is a precise sufficient regime for LINEAR TOTAL cost. Suppose
for a general full-dimensional K that

    h_Kr(e)=h_K+e phi_r+o(e) uniformly on the unit sphere,

where each phi_r is continuous. Then (1) has uniform support derivative
(1-t)phi_1+t phi_2, and its volume derivative is the corresponding
linear combination of the two volume derivatives. A direct proof uses
the exact mixed-volume telescoping identity

    |L|-|K|=(1/d) sum_(i=0)^(d-1)
       integral (h_L-h_K) dS(L[i],K[d-1-i]).              (11)

Divide by e. Uniform convergence of the integrand and weak continuity
of the mixed area measures make each term tend to integral phi dS_K;
the factor1/d cancels the d terms. This proves the claim without
asserting differentiability for arbitrary Hausdorff-Lipschitz paths.

This sufficient hypothesis is absent in(3), as just proved. Moreover
linear total cost alone does not automatically give linear FIXED CAP
costs: intersection with a cap is a separate operation and does not
commute with Minkowski averaging. A valid global minimax argument must
establish the required response-cone closure, including those cap
terms, rather than infer it solely from the exact compatibility(2).
